sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: Appointed after the **1896-97 Famine** which affected vast regions of the Bombay Presidency, Central Provinces, and Punjab.
• **Chairman**: Sir James Lyall, a seasoned colonial administrator.
• **Core Mandate**: To review the effectiveness of the **Famine Code** (1883) and suggest improvements in relief distribution and administrative preparedness.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The commission emphasized the need for 'Village Works' and the importance of 'Gratuitous Relief' for those unable to perform manual labor.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Shift from large public works to smaller, localized village-level works.
Administrative decentralization to prevent overcrowding in camps.
Emphasis on 'Suspension' and 'Remission' of land revenue.
Economic stability of the peasantry to prevent long-term indebtedness.
Mains: Critique of colonial economic drain.

items.definition: The foundational document established after the Strachey Commission; Lyall reviewed its implementation and suggested modifications for better efficiency.
Direct aid provided to the 'helpless' (elderly, infirm, children) who could not work on relief sites; Lyall advocated for its expansion.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Village Works**: Decentralized relief to keep laborers near their homes.
• **Revenue Policy**: Formalized the criteria for granting land revenue remissions during crop failure.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Colonial obsession with 'budgetary discipline' often undermined the scale of relief.
• **Solutions**: The commission paved the way for the MacDonnell Commission (1900) which further refined famine management.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-L-M' (Strachey, Lyall, MacDonnell).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chronological order of major Famine Commissions: Strachey (1880) -> Lyall (1898) -> MacDonnell (1900).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Lyall Commission (1898) with the MacDonnell Commission (1900). Remember: Lyall was for the 1896-97 famine; MacDonnell was for the 1899-1900 famine.

Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Administrative Paternalism' to describe the British approach to famine relief—it was reactive, not proactive, and focused on maintaining order rather than preventing starvation.

keyTakeaways: The Lyall Commission was a review body for the 1896-97 famine relief operations.
It advocated for decentralized village-level relief works over massive, centralized camps.
It solidified the administrative framework for land revenue remissions during natural calamities.
